 While many shows experience shakeups as networks make programming scheduling decisions, Fire Country has enjoyed a pretty stable schedule on CBS since it premiered in the 2023-2024 TV season. The series has remained largely undisturbed because it was a major hit at its premiere and quickly became a powerhouse anchor for the network's Friday night lineup, airing consistently at 9 pm ET. Co-created and led by SEAL Team fan favorite Max Thieriot as Bode Donovan, the firefighter drama became one of broadcast television's top-performing shows, drawing massive live and streaming audiences each week. Its reliable success and steady Friday night presence even allowed CBS to build an entire franchise around the fictional town of Edgewater , paving the way for its first official spin-off, Sheriff Country .

 However, that steady routine is changing dramatically for the 2026–2027 broadcast season. To make room for a more crowded scripted lineup, CBS has shaken up its Friday night schedule and trimmed Fire Country 's fifth season to a shortened 13-episode run, down from its usual 20-episode order. Rather than stretching across the traditional fall-to-spring television calendar, the firefighter drama is set to wrap up its season unusually early in February 2027 . Once Fire Country concludes its run, Sheriff Country will slide into the 9 p.m. time slot to clear space on the schedule for Matthew Gray Gubler 's new procedural, Einstein .
 Some more disappointing news for fans is that there will be no new episode of Fire Country this Friday, November 20. Instead, the series is entering an unexpected four-week fall hiatus, leaving viewers waiting until December 11 for the action in Edgewater to resume. This pause adds to the frustration of an already condensed season , cutting into the show's usual fall momentum just as storylines heat up. While CBS fills the Friday night gap with reruns and holiday programming, loyal viewers will have to be patient to see what emergency next rocks Edgewater and tests Station 42.

 You Are… 
 Tracker works because the case changes every week and the four people
 solving it never do. Here is which of them you are, what it says about you, and the case for yours
 being the best of the four.
 Justin Hartley · Tracker · CBS 
 Colter Shaw 
 You would rather handle it yourself and you are usually capable
 of doing so. Colter is a survivalist who lives in an Airstream and takes reward money for
 finding missing people, which is a premise that only works because he is clearly running
 from something of his own.
 You are competent and self-contained, and the people who love you find both of those
 slightly difficult.
 The show premiered after the Super Bowl in February 2024 and became the most watched new
 drama of that season.
 Justin Hartley came straight off This Is Us into it, which is about as hard a pivot as
 network TV offers.
 Your flaw is that handling everything yourself is a decision, not a personality, and
 people can tell.
 Fiona Rene · Tracker · CBS 
 Reenie Greene 
 You know somebody, and that somebody owes you a favour. Reenie is
 the lawyer Colter calls when a case needs a door opened legally, and she is the only person
 on the show who can get further with a phone call than he can on foot.
 Your network is your real skill, and you have been quietly building it for years.
 She was promoted to a series regular because the audience responded to her faster than
 anybody planned for.
 Every episode where she takes the lead is an argument that the show should let her do it
 more often.
 Your risk is that being the fixer for everybody leaves nobody fixing things for you.
 Eric Graise · Tracker · CBS 
 Bobby Exley 
 You are two steps ahead and you rarely mention it. Bobby is the
 one who finds the thing that unlocks the case, usually from a desk, usually about ninety
 seconds before anybody realises they needed it.
 You do the part of the work nobody sees and you are completely fine with that, mostly.
 Eric Graise brought the character in from the pilot and he has grown into the show's
 best deadpan.
 Every procedural needs this role and very few of them make it this watchable.
 Your weakness is assuming people have noticed what you did, because they have not.
 Jensen Ackles · Tracker · CBS 
 Russell Shaw 
 You turn up, change the temperature of the room, and leave people
 arguing about you. Russell is Colter's brother, ex-military, and the show has never once let
 the audience settle on whether he is a help or a problem, which is exactly why he keeps
 coming back.
 You are the most interesting person in most rooms and the hardest to plan around.
 Jensen Ackles arrived in the first season and the response was strong enough that CBS
 kept bringing him back.
 Fifteen years of Supernatural means he can play charming and unsettling in the same line
 reading.
 Your flaw is that keeping people guessing is fun for you and tiring for everybody else.

 In the December 11 episode titled "Fight the Future," the show picks up continuing storylines, including the new data center in Edgewater and Sharon's luck. But first, Station 42 races against time to save a man who has been buried in a frozen industrial accident. Meanwhile, Sharon ( Diane Farr ) finds herself trapped in a desperate life-or-death situation that threatens to expose a dangerous secret. Could this have something to do with the bag of money she found and has used part of, but the owner has come to reclaim?
 Catch the new episode on Friday, December 11, and stay tuned to Collider for more updates.
